‘Lifting Restrictions Must Not Become a Precedent,’ Kyiv Says After Russian Billionaires Delisted — Ukraine criticized the EU’s decision to remove Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list, warning it could weaken EU unity. But, Kyiv welcomed the bloc’s three-year extension of broader sanctions and plans new measures against Russian oligarchs.

Russia’s Jet Drone Use Explodes 8-Fold Since June, Ukraine Says — Ukraine’s air force said Russia’s use of jet-powered drones has risen drastically since June, going from 350 to 1,500 within a month, before reaching a peak of 2,850 in August. Around 1,900 launches have been documented in September so far, as Kyiv scrambles to produce enough jet-powered interceptors to meet the new challenge.

Ukraine’s Battle-Tested Drones Could Soon Be Made in America — Ukraine is ready to sign a landmark drone defense agreement with the US, CBS News reported on Tuesday, citing three people familiar with the negotiations. The framework would expand testing and production of Ukrainian military technology in America while transferring Kyiv’s battlefield expertise to US forces.

Russian Drones Over Kyiv – War of Speed and New Deep Strike Tactics — As Russia steps up its continuous attacks on civilian targets in Ukraine’s cities with increasing numbers of jet-powered Shahed drones, Ukraine is having to focus on adapting on current and future technological threats.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Command Posts, Rubicon Depot in the Donetsk, Luhansk Region — Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck Russian drone command posts, a Rubicon drone depot and military supply facilities in the Donetsk and Luhansk regions, Kyiv’s General Staff said. The strikes followed a Monday attack on a Russian drone launch and storage site in Russia’s Oryol region.

Germany Probes Drone and Suspected Explosives Near Air Base — A broken drone and suspected explosive material were found near the Bundeswehr’s Wunstorf Air Base in Lower Saxony. German investigators are checking whether the discovery is connected to the attempted explosive-drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport, where Ukrainian cargo aircraft were reportedly targeted.

Russia’s Global Recruitment Pipeline: How Russia Hunts the World’s Poor to Feed Its War in Ukraine – Part 1 — Russia has built an extensive recruitment pipeline targeting foreign nationals across Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Recruits are often lured with promises of civilian employment, education opportunities, or fast-tracked citizenship, only to be signed into military contracts and deployed to combat zones. Ukraine estimates at least 27,000 foreigners from more than 130 countries have ent

Russian Drone Attack on Kyiv Kills 2, Injures 22 as Explosions Rock Central Kyiv — Kyiv came under a Russian drone attack Wednesday morning, with at least five explosions reported near the Central Railway Station area. The station itself was not hit, Ukrzaliznytsia said. At least four people were wounded, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko.

‘Setting the Stage’: Russia May be Preparing to ‘Annex South Ossetia’ — Russia may be preparing to annex South Ossetia, according to analyst Goble, as uncertainty over its military base in Armenia changes Moscow’s calculations. The EU has called recent elections there null and void and warned of steps toward possible annexation.

Stubb: ‘You Guys Are Not Going to Win This’ – Putin Must Come to the Peace Table — Finnish President said Ukraine is in a stronger position than a year ago and that Russia is not winning the war. He called for Putin to come to the negotiating table and backed a reciprocal energy ceasefire before winter.

Russian Attack on Kyiv Kills 2, Injures 22 as Gas Stations and Infrastructure Hit — Russia launched 161 drones against Ukraine overnight, damaging warehouses, gas stations and transport infrastructure in Kyiv and injuring 22, killing 2. Two people were wounded in Zaporizhzhia, while eight, including a child, were injured in Izyum by four guided bombs.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 22, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 22, 2026.

Rubio to Meet Lavrov at UN as Putin Remains Absent Since Full-Scale Invasion — Rubio and Lavrov will meet in New York on Wednesday, with Lavrov representing Moscow at the UNGA as Putin remains absent from the gathering since launching the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

7 Takeaways From Zelensky’s New York Press Conference After Trump Meeting — After meeting Donald Trump in New York, Zelensky detailed Ukraine’s energy ceasefire proposal, readiness for trilateral talks, Patriot needs, sanctions leverage and concerns over Russian pressure on Europe.

Zelensky Warns Putin May Attack NATO Country to Distract From Heavy Losses at Home — Zelensky warned that Putin could escalate against NATO countries to distract from Russia’s battlefield failures, intimidate Europe and weaken Western support for Ukraine.

US, Iran Hold First Direct Talks in Months After Trump Threatens ‘Annihilation’ — US and Iranian officials resumed face-to-face talks in New York for the first time in months, with Trump saying another meeting is planned as Tehran sets conditions for a broader deal.

Zelensky, UK Prime Minister Burnham Meet in New York as Kyiv Warns Russia Preparing Massive Attack — On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York Zelensky and Burnham discussed air defense, winter preparations and sanctions as Kyiv warned that Russia is preparing another major attack.

Zelensky Offers Energy Truce as Trump Signals Support for Patriot Production in Ukraine — President Volodymyr Zelensky met with US President Donald Trump during the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. Ukraine offered a reciprocal energy ceasefire should Russia halt attacks on its power grid, while Trump signaled openness to licensing Patriot interceptor production in Ukraine.

Europe Warned It Is Running Out of Time to Prepare for Wider War With Russia — Speakers at a Kyiv conference warned that Europe may already be losing the hybrid war with Russia and remains unprepared for a wider conflict. They called for stronger European defense, faster military production and a central role for Ukraine.

Hungary-Ukraine Diplomatic Relations Strain Further as Magyar Likens C8 to Village Football — Hungary’s Prime Minister Péter Magyar defended Budapest’s decision not to join Ukraine’s Carpathian Eight (C8) initiative launched on Friday, Sept. 18, which was initially presented as comprising Hungary. Budapest confirmed that it received – and declined – the invitation to join on Monday, before comparing its inclusion without consent to being assigned to a village football team and having to provide

Trump Says Putin Is Willing to Meet as Diplomatic Momentum Continues — US President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin is willing to meet and wants the war in Ukraine to end. Trump made his remarks during a meeting with US officials and President Volodymyr Zelensky at the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday, describing Washington’s recent efforts to broker an end to Russia’s war as productive.

Zelensky Condemns Delistings of Russian Oligarchs in Western Sanctions — During his meeting with European Commission President Ursula Von der Leyen, President Volodymyr Zelensky said proposals to remove Russian oligarchs from EU sanction lists are “suicidal and counterproductive,” linking the warning to Russia’s continued missile and drone barrage on Ukraine nationwide. The talks also centered on sustaining Ukraine’s budget and defense needs through 2027.

Erdoğan Backs Peace Upholding Ukraine’s Territorial Integrity — During the opening of the high-level debates of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan called on Russia’s full-scale invasion to end, with Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity preserved. His statement came as Turkey remains Russia’s third-largest fossil fuel buyer.

Russia Attempts to Infiltrate Ukraine Through Pipeline from Kursk — Over the past week, Russian troops tried twice to use a major cross-border gas pipeline to penetrate northern Ukraine from Russia’s Kursk region. According to the Institute for the Study of War, both attempts failed.

Trump’s Message to Putin: ‘Settle the War’ — Speaking at the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday, US President Donald Trump used his address to urge an end to Russia’s war against Ukraine and warned that Washington could use new tariff powers against Moscow’s energy buyers. His remarks came ahead of a meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Commander Warns Russian Groups Could Reach Zaporizhzhia — Dmytro Filatov, commander of the 1st Separate Assault Regiment, said Russia could attempt to infiltrate Zaporizhzhia with small infantry groups during the winter. Ukraine’s Southern Grouping rejected claims that a direct Russian advance into the city is highly likely, while previous warnings about the southern front also did not lead to an assault on Zaporizhzhia.

EU to Extend Russia Sanctions After Latvia Drops Opposition to Oligarch Delistings — Latvia has backed down from opposing the delisting of two Russian oligarchs from EU sanctions, a decision pushed by France and Slovakia, ultimately paving the way for the extension of the EU’s sanctions against Russia hours before they are set to expire.

275,000 Missing in Russia-Ukraine War, Red Cross Says — About 275,000 people have been registered as missing in connection with Russia’s war against Ukraine, with the ICRC recording roughly 10,000 new cases each month.

Drone Near US Navy Air Defense Unit in Poland Prompts Polish Military 112 Call — An unauthorized drone flew near a US-operated missile defense base in northern Poland, prompting a military officer to call the emergency number 112, in accordance with procedures for incidents outside the base. Poland’s Defense Ministry said the drone remained under control and did not approach sensitive facilities.

Russia's Ex-National Guard Uniform Chief Jailed for 8 Years Over $70,000 Bribe — A Russian court has sentenced a colonel from Rosgvardiya to eight years in prison for taking a 6 million-ruble ($71,134) bribe from a contractor who never fulfilled its multibillion-ruble contract. The man is stripped of his military rank and the bribe money, in addition to receiving a court-mandated 6.7 million ruble ($79,430) fine.

Rubio Says Ukraine Targeted US-Linked Ships: What We Know — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Ukrainian forces repeatedly targeted vessels linked to the US, possibly unintentionally. Public reporting confirms that Washington previously asked Kyiv to avoid attacks on non-Russian tankers and infrastructure connected to US energy companies, but does not show that US-flagged or US-owned ships were repeatedly hit.

India Reportedly Eyes Cut in Russian Crude Over US Sanctions Concerns — India is said to be eyeing a cut in Russian crude imports after the US signed a new sanctions bill imposing 100% tariffs on Russian oil purchasers. The US introduced similar 50% tariffs on India last year before dropping them to 18%, after which imports doubled within a month and peaked at nearly 3 million barrels per day in July, many of which made their way back to Russia as gasoline amid an ongoing fuel crisis.

Naftogaz, ORLEN Sign New LNG, $500 Million Petroleum Product Supply Deals — Naftogaz Group and its subsidiary Ukrnafta signed two memoranda with Poland’s ORLEN during the Carpathian Eight Summit, securing three LNG shipments for the first quarter of 2027 and up to $500 million in petroleum product supplies. The deals also open the door to exporting Ukrainian crude oil for processing in Central Europe, extending a network of import routes Ukraine built after Russian strikes cut domestic gas produ

Russian Ex-Mayor Who Left Prison for Ukraine War Dies From Combat Wounds — A former Russian mayor convicted of accepting luxury cars as a bribe was reportedly killed after signing a defense ministry contract that allowed him to leave custody and fight against Ukraine.

Molfar Intelligence Launches AI-Powered Platform to Track Information Threats — Minos brings monitoring, risk assessment, people profiling, analyst-led research and response coordination into one environment for enterprises and governments. It is built on thousands of cases worked by Molfar Intelligence analysts.

‘The World Is Bigger Than Five’ – Turkey’s Erdogan Calls for Abolition of UN Veto — Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has called for abolishing the UN Security Council’s veto and ending permanent membership, arguing the system no longer reflects today’s world. He proposed rotating elected members and a stronger General Assembly, reviving debate over a structure largely unchanged since 1945.

Ukraine's Drone Forces Hit 300 Russian Shadow Fleet Tankers in 3 Months — The commander of Ukraine’s drone forces said his branch has struck 300 Russian shadow fleet tankers within 11 weeks – 134 in the Sea of Azov and 166 in the Black Sea – in an operation dubbed “Operation MoLoChKa.” He previously put the tally at 218 struck by early August, with most vessels attacked in July, when the operation began.

Ukraine to Charge Russia in UN for Causing Humanitarian Disaster in Occupied City — Ukraine FM Sybiha urges UN intervention as Russia creates humanitarian catastrophe in occupied Oleshky (Kherson): 2,000+ civilians, incl. children, lack food, water, services; blocked aid/evacuation; people forage grass; FPV drones hunt them. Kremlin acknowledges crisis, blames Ukraine. Red Cross ready but barred.

Ukraine Hits Major Russian Drone Hub 175 Kilometers From Border, Damages 5 Launchers — Ukraine hit a Russian complex in the Oryol region used to store, prepare and launch attack UAVs, Kyiv’s General Staff said. At least three storage facilities were hit and five launchers were damaged.

Plot to Kill Russian Dissident: SBU Detains Hitwoman Sent via Belarus — Ukraine’s Security Service detained a woman accused of preparing to assassinate a Russian opposition figure who fought for Ukraine and now leads a nationwide civic organization. The SBU said Russia’s FSB recruited and trained the suspect in occupied Melitopol before sending her to Kyiv through Belarus.

Putin Plans to Visit APEC Summit, May Skip Trump’s G20 — Vladimir Putin plans to attend the APEC summit hosted by Xi Jinping in China but is likely to skip Donald Trump’s G20 gathering in Florida, Bloomberg reported on Monday. His expected absence would also eliminate a possible venue for direct talks with Volodymyr Zelensky.

Ukraine Arrests Lviv Student for Registering Starlink Terminals for Russian Troops — Ukraine said it arrested a student in Lviv and his friend for activating at least 14 Starlink terminals for Russia, and potentially at least 40 more. The case is the latest in a series of cases in which Russia has tried to recruit Ukrainians to activate Starlink terminals after Kyiv’s new verification system in February, while Russia’s alternative, Rassvet, continues to suffer troubled launches.

Latvia Blocks EU Bid to Lift Oligarch Sanctions — Latvia blocked an EU compromise that would lift sanctions on Russian-linked billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman while renewing restrictions on roughly 3,000 other individuals and entities for three years. The sanctions require unanimous approval from all 27 EU members and are due to expire at midnight on Tuesday, unless an agreement is reached.

Sybiha: Belarus Helps Russia Carry Out Drone Attacks on Ukraine — Andrii Sybiha accused Lukashenko’s regime of directly supporting Russian drone attacks and backed sanctions proposed by Belarusian democratic leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya.

Black Sea Blockade Threatens Global Food Shock — Russian and Ukrainian wheat exports during the July-to-September harvest period are expected to fall to roughly half last year’s volume as attacks disrupt Black Sea shipping. The crisis has pushed wheat prices to three-year highs, strained Ukraine’s storage capacity and increased food-security risks for countries dependent on affordable grain.

France to Strengthen Ukraine’s Air Defense With Radars, Interceptors — France will supply Ukraine with radars and interceptor missiles as Kyiv faces intensified threats to its energy system ahead of winter. Macron’s announcement came after talks with Zelensky in New York and follows discussions with Trump on air defense, an energy-strike moratorium and possible peace negotiations.

Ukrainian Forces Use New STING S Interceptor to Down Russian Geran-5 — Ukraine’s new STING S interceptor has shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran-5. The system is undergoing combat trials, with Wild Hornets planning mass production after testing.

Stay – and Lose Control: Auchan, Nestlé and Leroy Merlin in Russia — Russian assets of Auchan and Nestlé, as well as the legacy Leroy Merlin, were transferred to the temporary management. The KSE Institute contrasts these cases with companies such as Unilever, H&M and McDonald’s, which accepted significant exit costs but completed their withdrawal from Russia.
CARTOON: The Way Sanctions Should Work — Serhii Kolyada’s ironic take on the latest international events.

Moldova Seeks Energy, Water Emergency Over Critically Low Dnister Levels — Moldova is seeking emergency powers as critically low Dnister River levels threaten water and energy supplies. Authorities warn of potential shortages as the country remains reliant on imported energy, while the river’s decline has been compounded by drought, irrigation needs, and a Russian strike on a Ukrainian hydropower facility.

Ukrainian Drone Swarm Strikes Key Russian Oil Refinery in Samara — Dozens of Ukrainian drones targeted industrial facilities in Russia’s Samara Oblast overnight, reportedly striking a major Rosneft refinery and triggering a large fire, as Kyiv continues its campaign against Russia’s oil-refining infrastructure.

US Army Acquires Long-Range Ukrainian Surveillance Drones in $10.6m Deal — The U.S. Army will acquire Ukrainian-developed Raybird reconnaissance drones under a $10.64 million contract with Skyeton. The drones, capable of 24-hour flights and long-range surveillance, have been used extensively by Ukraine for intelligence and targeting. The deal highlights Ukraine’s growing expertise and expanding defense industry, shaped by extensive battlefield experience in drone warfare.

Zelensky Meets CIA Chief John Ratcliffe in Ireland En Route to New York – Reuters — Zelensky met CIA Director John Ratcliffe in Ireland while traveling to New York for the UN General Assembly, according to Reuters.
Zelensky, Macron Discuss Energy Moratorium Ahead of Trump Meeting — Zelensky met Macron in New York as Kyiv pushes for stronger air defense and reciprocal de-escalation ahead of talks with Trump.

Russian Ballistic Strikes Hit Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad, Kill 4 — Russian forces struck industrial sites in Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad during an overnight ballistic attack, killing two and wounding three people in Dnipro.

Macron, Trump Discuss Interceptors for Ukraine and Energy Truce — Macron pressed Trump for faster missile interceptors for Ukraine and discussed a possible reciprocal moratorium on Russian and Ukrainian energy strikes.

Tsikhanouskaya Warns Against Belarus Trade as Trump Looks Beyond Canada for Potash — Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya warned Washington against expanding trade with Minsk as Trump pursues a major Belarusian potash deal aimed at securing supplies for less than the US currently pays Canada.

Moscow Oil Refinery Halts Crude Processing After Sunday’s Drone Strike — Russia’s Moscow Oil Refinery has halted crude processing after a Ukrainian drone strike damaged key units at the facility. Zelensky said the attack targeted oil and logistics infrastructure supporting Russia’s war effort.

Ukraine Repels 197 Russian Attacks on Monday — According to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU), Russia launched 197 attacks over a 24-hour period ending 10:00 p.m. local time on Monday, Sept. 21, focusing on the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka axes. Thousands of kamikaze drones and at least 168 aerial guided bombs (KABs) were used by Russian armed forces to launch a sweeping barrage.

Hungary Refuses to Join Ukraine’s C8 Cooperation Initiative — Ukraine launched the new Carpathian Eight (C8) cooperation initiative to deepen security, energy and investment with regional members on Friday. While initial reports named Hungary as a member, the country’s Prime Minister Péter Magyar said Monday that Budapest declined the invitation and will not join the format. Hungary’s Foreign Ministry confirmed the position.

Ousted Prosecutor General Kravchenko Resigns From Prosecution Service — After “Operation Carthage” reached senior officials in his office, Ruslan Kravchenko lost the leadership post of prosecutor general. However, he remained a prosecutor until his latest resignation on Monday, even as President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree ousting him mid-September.

Ukraine Sets New Hospital Rules Amid New Two-Level Air Raid Alert System — Ukraine’s government has approved new rules for hospitals operating under the newly imposed two-level air raid alert system. During yellow (drone) alerts, facilities may remain open, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said. Red (missile threats, mass strikes and ballistic attacks) alerts require immediate sheltering, however, interrupting surgery, intensive care, resuscitation or emergency services for critically ill patient

EU Extends Russia Sanctions for 3 Years, Delists 2 Oligarchs — While EU ambassadors have finally agreed to extend sanctions on nearly 3,000 Russian individuals and entities after several failed attempts, the new sanctions will not include the previously disputed oligarchs, Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman. The decision has raised frustration among member states, while Kyiv condemned the move as unacceptable.

Russian Attack Destroys Pet Retailer Warehouse in Kyiv Region — A Russian overnight missile and drone attack destroyed a major warehouse belonging to Suziria Group in the Kyiv region. Company co-owner Polina Kosharna confirmed that no employees were injured during the strike, though emergency services remain at the scene to evaluate the full scale of the damage.

Russia Destroys Ukrainian Production Facility of World-Leading Ventilation Systems — In the early morning of Sept. 20, a Russian drone and missile attack destroyed the main Kyiv-region manufacturing facilities of Vents. As a global leader in ventilation equipment, the company is now assessing the severe damage to restore its production and logistics operations.

Russia ‘Unfortunately Lost Control’ of Its Diesel Refineries, Trump Says — Trump said on Monday that Russia has “unfortunately lost control” over its diesel production and called for the war to end. The comments came a day after a call with Zelensky and a day before the two’s meeting, with Trump having previously attempted to pin the blame for rising global diesel prices on Ukrainian strikes.

Russia’s ‘Partial Mobilization’ Turns 4: Is Another Draft Coming? — Four years after Vladimir Putin announced “partial mobilization,” Russia relies primarily on contract recruitment but also uses conscripts, prisoners, regional quotas, and administrative pressure to sustain its war. Ukrainian intelligence says slowing recruitment could push the Kremlin toward another call-up after the State Duma election, although no final decision has been independently confirmed.

Kernel Pilots Modular Grain Storage to Cushion Export Disruptions — Kernel installed the first modular grain store developed by a Ukrainian manufacturer at its request and filled it with 3,400 metric tons within two days. The company wrote that the design holds 3.5 times more than polymer grain bags in the same area. Kernel has bought units to add 40,000 tons of storage, which it plans to open to other producers.

EU Threatens Sanctions Over Russia’s Sham Elections in Occupied Ukraine — The EU condemned Russia’s parliamentary elections in occupied parts of Ukraine as a violation of international law and pledged sanctions against those involved in staging the vote.

Fedorov Says Zelensky Rejected His Election Proposal Because Zaluzhny Would Run — Former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said he personally proposed holding presidential elections in June and that President Zelensky was initially prepared to proceed. According to Fedorov, the president later abandoned the idea because former army chief Valery Zaluzhny would have entered the race.

US Army Buys Battle-Tested Ukraine Observation Drone — The US Army awarded Skyeton $10.64 million for Raybird reconnaissance drones, Ukraine’s first major military-drone export to the US. The Raybird is combat-proven, while another Ukrainian UAV, the F10, underwent US Army testing.

Russia Hits 2 Gas Stations on Kyiv-Lviv M06 Highway — The highway served as an artery between Kyiv and the country’s western border, with both gas stations hit on the section within the Zhytomyr region west of Kyiv. The attacks followed Russia’s escalated campaign against Ukrainian gas stations.

Moscow Fortifies Power Plant After Record Ukrainian Attack — Moscow’s CHP-8 power plant is being surrounded with concrete blocks that could support anti-drone netting, according to eyewitnesses cited by ASTRA. The work follows the largest reported Ukrainian aerial attack on Moscow, which damaged the Russian capital’s major oil refinery.

After State Elections: Can Merz Keep His Job? — Germany’s CDU suffered major losses in state elections in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, while Die Linke and AfD gained ground. The results have intensified questions over Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s leadership and the stability of Germany’s political centre. European media warn that growing polarisation could affect Germany’s role in Europe and support for Ukraine.

Ukraine Urges Europe to Send Patriot Missiles Now, Replenish Stocks With Future Production — Ukraine is proposing that European countries transfer Patriot missiles from existing stockpiles and replace them later with newly produced interceptors. Kyiv is also seeking faster access to bilateral funding commitments as the cost of the war rises.

Drones Target Major Russian Oil Hub 1,600 Kilometers From Ukraine — Drones reportedly attacked Ufa in Russia’s Bashkortostan region on Monday, potentially targeting oil infrastructure belonging to Bashneft, one of Russia’s largest refining complexes.

Book Genocide: How Russia Has Waged War on Ukrainian Books for Centuries — Russia’s campaign against Ukrainian books has a long history – from bans on publishing to modern attacks on the country’s publishing infrastructure. In the summer of 2026 alone, at least 9.65 million books were destroyed. For Ukraine, this is not only an economic loss but a threat to its cultural ecosystem.

EU Fails to Agree on Putin Sanctions Renewal — EU ambassadors again failed to agree on extending individual sanctions against nearly 3,000 people and entities linked to Russia’s aggression against Ukraine. The restrictions covering Vladimir Putin and other senior Russian officials are due to expire on Tuesday, unless all 27 member states approve their renewal.

Ukrainian Combat Medics Show Sweden How Drones Save Lives — Combat medics from Ukraine’s 1st Separate Medical Battalion took their MAUL armored unmanned ground vehicle to Sweden where they shared their techniques for using the technology to rescue casualties from within the “kill zone” on the modern battlefield.

Russian Strike Torches Historic Zaporizhzhia Heritage University — An overnight Russian attack on southern Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia burned down Building 3 of the city’s main university. Built in 1903, the building was said to be one of the university’s oldest historical landmarks, with the university hinting at “challenging” plans to restore it.

Russia Committed Nearly 900 Sexual Violence Crimes in Ukraine — Ukraine’s foreign minister said Russia uses rape and sexual violence as weapons of war, citing a UN report that documented 892 violations by Russian forces since February 2022.

Kremlin Says No Progress in Ukraine Peace Talks — Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said there had been no progress in negotiations to end Russia’s war against Ukraine, but Moscow hoped trilateral talks involving the US would resume. His comments came as President Volodymyr Zelensky and US President Trump prepare to meet in New York.

Frontline Update, Lyman Details, AFU Reorganization — The front line has moved in Ukraine’s favor in the northern Lyman sector, whereas the southern city of Orikhiv, in the Zaporizhzhia region, is bracing itself for an expected Russian push. Meanwhile the Dopropillya sector remains one of the hottest, with the 1st Corps honing its drone buzz saw under serious pressure.

Russia Plans 28,000 More Shahed-Type Drones a Year as It Expands Carbon-Fiber Plant — Russia is expanding a Rosatom carbon-fiber plant in Tatarstan that could enable production of an additional 28,000 Shahed-type attack drones annually. The expansion is part of Moscow’s broader push to increase domestic drone production, raising concerns over intensified attacks on Ukraine and growing security risks for Europe.

Romania Detains Pro-Russian Georgescu in Fraud Probe — Romanian investigators stopped pro-Russian former presidential candidate Călin Georgescu in traffic and took him in for questioning in an organized crime and fraud investigation. Prosecutors allege that a group posing as wealthy financiers obtained more than €1.1 million from a victim by promising multimillion-euro business loans.

Zelensky, Trump Agree to Meet in New York as Ukraine-US Peace Efforts Gain ‘Momentum’ — Zelensky and Trump agreed to meet in New York, as per the Ukrainian president. He described the talks as important and said the sides were discussing de-escalation, security, and humanitarian issues.

‘Disaster’: Far-Right Tops Another German State Vote as Merz’s CDU Routed in Worst Result in Decades — The AfD led Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania with 38.2% in exit polls, ahead of the Social Democrats at 35.5%.
